title: Sentinel Managed Security Incident Response Retainer: Hours Ledger, Rollover and Overage
content:
Each Sentinel Managed Security subscription keeps an incident response hours ledger, holding the retainer hours available in the current contract year.

## Grants

At activation and on each anniversary of the term start date, the subscription is granted the tier's annual included incident response hours for the new contract year.

## Draws and overage

Hours logged on an engaged incident are drawn from the current contract year's balance up to what remains. The balance of a contract year is the hours granted for that contract year, whether as the annual grant or as a rollover, less the hours drawn and the hours forfeited for that contract year; the contract year used is the one containing the incident's closure. Hours beyond the balance are invoiced as an overage at the tier's overage hourly rate per hour, rounded half up to the cent. The overage is invoiced once per incident, in the month of the incident's closure.

| Hours logged on the incident (hypothetical) | Balance of the contract year | Hours drawn | Overage hours | Overage at a hypothetical 200.00 USD per hour |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | 6 | 4 | 0 | None |
| 5 | 3 | 3 | 2 | 400.00 USD |
| 3 | 0 | 0 | 3 | 600.00 USD |

## Contract-year end

At a contract year's end, unused hours up to the tier's rollover share of the annual included hours are granted into the next year as a rollover, and the rest are forfeited. Rolled-over hours never roll a second time.

Illustration with hypothetical figures: an annual grant of 40 hours and a rollover share of 25 percent allow at most 10 hours to roll. If 16 hours are unused at year end, 10 are granted into the next year and 6 are forfeited; if 7 hours are unused, all 7 are granted into the next year and none is forfeited. With a rollover share of 0 percent, every unused hour is forfeited.

## Closing

At closing all remaining hours are forfeited and never refunded.
